items.subject: Global reduction hierarchy and launch-count alternatives
items.objective: Explore global reduction hierarchy and launch count, treating fewer launches as a hypothesis rather than a requirement. For the primary comparisons, keep the baseline intra-block reduction fixed so this tree isolates global topology. Compare a two-kernel design (input partials, then finalization writing directly to out) with a design that adds a parallel partial-reduction stage or retains a recursive hierarchy when a single-CTA finalizer has too much work. Tune tile size and partial count, and compare full-call performance rather than attributing gains from launch count alone. Handle all valid n generically; do not scan the entire large input in one CTA or specialize to listed test sizes. Use only the supplied scratch and default stream, without relying on scratch initialization. Ensure intermediate sums are exact under cancellation using int64 intermediates or proven-safe bounds, and narrow only after the true total is established. Validate all required inputs, report failed variants, and provide repeated measurements.
